facts.fact: COMESA's half-year report states that Component 1 (USD 36 million) of the USD 65 million Digital Eswatini Project (P508948) supports expansion of the national broadband backbone to connect schools, health centres and Tinkhundla centres; in January-June 2026 the project was in preparation only, with the infrastructure assessment begun and no centre reported connected.
facts.system: Digital Eswatini Project, Component 1: backbone expansion to connect Tinkhundla centres

facts.fact: The Digital Eswatini Project that is to connect Tinkhundla centres is financed by a World Bank IBRD loan and IDA credit of USD 65 million, approved in June 2026, with a USD 2 million World Bank preparation grant closing December 2026, per COMESA's half-year report; no domestic budget line is stated.
facts.system: Digital Eswatini Project, Component 1: backbone expansion to connect Tinkhundla centres

facts.fact: The Digital Eswatini Project is implemented by the Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology, whose six-specialist Project Implementation Unit became operational on 1 January 2026, per COMESA's half-year report.
facts.system: Digital Eswatini Project, Component 1: backbone expansion to connect Tinkhundla centres

facts.fact: World Bank grant negotiations for the Digital Eswatini Project concluded on 18 May 2026 and the loan was approved in June 2026; the project, which is to connect Tinkhundla centres among other sites, had not reached loan effectiveness and full implementation was expected in 2027, per COMESA's half-year report.
facts.system: Digital Eswatini Project, Component 1: backbone expansion to connect Tinkhundla centres

facts.fact: COMESA's report for January-June 2026 gives no Tinkhundla centre or other local office as connected under the Digital Eswatini Project: Eswatini 'focused on project preparation', and the assessment mapping the national backbone was still to be finalised in the third quarter of 2026.
